region: Serra do Mar transition forest / Parana, Brazil
conditions: 16-21 C / intermittent mist / light southeast wind
summary: Four stratified transects sampled the forest edge, closed-canopy interior, riparian corridor, and a regenerating slope. Timed visual encounter surveys were paired with acoustic and leaf-litter searches.
primaryFinding: Species richness remained high at the forest edge, but moisture-sensitive amphibians were concentrated in the shaded riparian transect.
methods: Observers completed two 200 m passes per transect at dawn and after dusk. Records required a photograph, diagnostic call, or agreement by two observers. Plot canopy was estimated at five fixed points.
limitations: Heavy mist reduced detectability during the second evening survey. Counts describe encounter frequency rather than population size, and cryptic leaf-litter taxa are probably underrepresented.
recommendation: Protect the riparian corridor as a no-disturbance buffer, retain coarse woody debris, and repeat the survey in the wet season before approving new trail work.

actions.action: Establish a 30 m no-disturbance buffer along the riparian transect.
Suspend new trail grading until wet-season amphibian surveys are complete.
Retain fallen timber and deep leaf litter in edge restoration plots.
Repeat acoustic and encounter surveys after peak seasonal rainfall.
